intro: This awareness course covered hazards and risks, the law behind assessment, the HSE five steps, the hierarchy of control, and positive risk-taking.
points: This is awareness only; formal risk assessments are carried out and signed off by a manager or competent person, not by you.
Risk assessment is a legal requirement under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and the Management Regulations 1999.
You have your own legal duties: take reasonable care, follow safe systems, use equipment properly, and report hazards and concerns.
If a safe system cannot be followed because equipment is missing or broken, stop and report it rather than working around it.
Work down the hierarchy of control — eliminate the hazard first; PPE is the last line because it protects only the wearer.
Use dynamic risk assessment in the moment and support positive risk-taking, respecting the unwise but capable choices people make about their lives.
